These are fictional adaptation illustrations, not portraits or photographs of real source subjects. Cast/design continuity: Three unrelated fictional diarists with clearly separate faces, clothes, rooms and lives, not portraits of real subjects. AMANDA: auburn shoulder-length curls, rust cardigan, small lavender bedroom and wooden desk. JUAN: short dark hair, teal shirt, pale-blue room with a large square window and recorder on sill. MELISSA: dark hair in a bun, mustard blouse, warm ochre domestic room with her own small son in blue. Two frames per person: youth then adulthood. Never put diarists together or transfer a child between accounts.. CELL 0: AMANDA ONLY, first independent account. A young person with auburn curls and rust cardigan sits at a wooden desk in a small lavender bedroom, one hand poised over a plain cassette recorder and the other resting open on the desk. Uncertain glance toward the room door; no other diarist, child or shared event. CELL 1: AMANDA ONLY years later, same recognizable auburn curls now slightly greying, rust-brown cardigan, her own quiet lavender-toned room. She listens to her own plain cassette recorder with hand resting beside its buttons, eyes registering gradual recognition. No Juan, Melissa, borrowed child or composite family. CELL 2: JUAN ONLY, second independent account. A short-dark-haired young man in teal sits beside a large square window in a pale-blue room, looking toward the daylight with one hand steadying a cassette recorder on the wide sill. Grounded chair, coherent arm contact, his own distinct room and question about the future. CELL 3: JUAN ONLY years later, same recognizable face and dark hair lightly greying, deeper teal shirt in his own pale-blue room near the same kind of square window. He listens thoughtfully to his own recorder, shoulders lowered, one hand on the sill. No other diarist, reunion or invented life event. CELL 4: MELISSA ONLY, third independent account. Young mother with dark hair in bun and mustard blouse sits in a warm ochre room beside her own small son in blue, speaking toward a plain recorder on a low table while turning a little toward him. Safe natural child posture, distinct domestic setting; the future addressee is her child. CELL 5: MELISSA ONLY years later in her own ochre room. The same mother, visibly older but recognizable, sits beside her teenage son, now taller with the same dark hair and blue clothing cue. They listen together to her recorder, a small mutual glance linking only these two. Neither Amanda nor Juan is present. Editorial limit: Exactly two dedicated scenes per account. Keep Amanda, Juan and Melissa distinct, with Melissa alone having the child/teen son. No blended biography, synchronized shared event or voice impersonation.
